image_description: A close-up, slightly blurry photograph of a vintage aneroid barometer. The image focuses on the circular dial face, which features concentric rings of numerical markings (likely inches of mercury and millibars) and weather condition text. A central brass mechanism is visible with multiple thin black pointer hands extending outwards. The casing appears to be dark wood or metal with a glass cover, showing reflections.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The numbers on the outer and inner scales are not distinct digits but rather warped shapes that mimic the form of numbers. They are illegible and structurally nonsensical upon close inspection.

The pointer hands emerge from the center in a physically ambiguous way. They appear to float or merge with the background brass mechanism without a clear pivot point or consistent thickness. One hand seems to fade out before reaching the edge.
The white surface of the dial has a smeared, painterly texture rather than the smooth, printed finish of a real instrument. The printed lines vary in sharpness inconsistently.
